question: What is the mechanism of action of pembrolizumab?

route.reason: Mechanism of action is a drug label section (FDA label content), not trial registry data.

draft.text: Pembrolizumab is a monoclonal antibody that binds to the PD-1 receptor and blocks its interaction with PD-L1 and PD-L2, releasing PD-1 pathway-mediated inhibition of the immune response, including the anti-tumor immune response [label:pembrolizumab:mechanism_of_action:0]. Binding of PD-L1 and PD-L2 to PD-1 on T cells normally inhibits T cell proliferation and cytokine production [label:pembrolizumab:mechanism_of_action:0]. Some tumors upregulate PD-1 ligands, and signaling through this pathway can contribute to inhibition of active T-cell immune surveillance of tumors [label:pembrolizumab:mechanism_of_action:0]. In syngeneic mouse tumor models, blocking PD-1 activity decreased tumor growth [label:pembrolizumab:mechanism_of_action:0].
